articles.title: Watch: 'Shaken and emotional' passengers arrive in Israel after Flydubai incident
articles.summary: The BBC's Yogita Limaye is at Ben Gurion Airport as passengers from the Flydubai flight arrive in Israel.
articles.body:
Passengers from the diverted Flydubai flight to Israel have arrived at Ben Gurion Airport following a stabbing incident earlier on Wednesday.

A pilot on an Israel-bound flight stabbed another pilot and "apparently tried to crash the plane", Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said, with the flight later being diverted to Saudi Arabia.

The BBC's Yogita Limaye is at Ben Gurion Airport as passengers arrive.

articles.title: FATO OU FAKE: Debate Globo com candidatos ao Governo de PE no 1º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Participaram do debate desta terça-feira (29) Ivan Moraes (PSOL), João Campos (PSB) e Raquel Lyra (PSD).
articles.summary: Participaram do debate desta terça-feira (29) Ivan Moraes (PSOL), João Campos (PSB) e Raquel Lyra (PSD).
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo de PE: João Campos (PSB), Ivan Moraes (PSOL) e Raquel Lyra (PSD) — Foto: Brenda Alcântara/Globo

A Globo promoveu, nesta terça-feira (29), um debate com candidatos ao Governo de Pernambuco. Com mediação do jornalista Márcio Bonfim, o encontro, realizado nos estúdios da TV Globo no Recife, foi transmitido ao vivo pela emissora e pelo g1 .

Os participantes, em ordem alfabética, foram:

A equipe do Fato ou Fake checou as principais declarações dos candidatos. Leia:

"A Caatinga é um bioma tão importante, responsável pela absorção de quase metade do carbono de todo o Brasil."

De 2015 a 2022, a caatinga foi responsável por quase 50% de toda a captura de carbono do Brasil, de acordo com um estudo feito por cientistas da Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp), divulgado em setembro de 2025.

O trabalho, conduzido pelo pesquisador Luís Miguel da Costa, ao lado do professor Newton La Scala Jr., foi publicado na revista científica "Science of the Total Environment" e analisa o período de 2015 a 2022.

Segundo a pesquisa, o semiárido nordestino se mostrou um aliado na regulação climática e no cumprimento das metas de emissões líquidas zero assumidas pelo Brasil no Acordo de Paris.

O estudo também avaliou que o bioma apresentou crescimento na atividade fotossintética em anos mais chuvosos, elevando de forma significativa a sua capacidade de sequestro de carbono.

O desemprego em Pernambuco está em terceiro lugar todas as unidades da federação, com uma taxa de 8,3%, segundo a Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Contínua (Pnad Contínua) do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) do segundo trimestre de 2026 , divulgada em 14 de agosto.

Pernambuco divide o terceiro lugar com o Piauí e está atrás da Bahia (9,1%) e do Amapá, que lidera o ranking com uma taxa de desemprego de 9,8%.

Procurada pelo Fato ou Fake , a assessoria do candidato informou que ele se referia especificamente ao recorte etário da população acima dos 40 anos.

"O que não dá é para a gente assistir ao que a gente viu, inclusive um uma chefe de estado falar sobre uma esterilização forçada numa ala pediátrica de hospital."

A governadora Raquel Lyra (PSD) apareceu em um vídeo, filmado em maio de 2025, dizendo para ser feita uma laqueadura numa mulher sem que a paciente soubesse da cirurgia.

As imagens foram gravadas na inauguração da Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) do Hospital Regional Dom Moura, em Garanhuns, no Agreste de Pernambuco, e divulgadas na imprensa em 20 de setembro deste ano.

Após a divulgação do caso, a candidata à reeleição em Pernambuco pediu desculpas publicamente por meio de nota e de um vídeo em sua conta no Instagram. Ela afirmou que a afirmação "foi uma fala equivocada" e que não "traduz o respeito" que tem pelas mulheres.

“Vamos levar isso para Pernambuco, inclusive as creches, onde ela prometeu 250, não fez nem 15 e, na cidade do Recife, a gente fez mais de 107".

Selo Não é Bem Assim (Horizontal) — Foto: g1

Em entrevista ao g1 em outubro de 2022, antes de ser eleita governadora de Pernambuco, Raquel Lyra prometeu a construção de 250 creches em sua gestão . Na terça-feira (29), o governo inaugurou a 23ª creche das unidades prometidas para o estado, em Tacaratu, no Sertão, e afirmou que pretende, até o fim do ano, entregar 100 unidades.

Já em Recife, apesar de João Campos afirmar ter entregado mais de 107 creches, apenas 15 unidades foram, de fato, feitas pela gestão ao longo dos seus dois mandatos como prefeito de Recife, entre 2021 e 2026. As outras 92 não foram inauguradas pela gestão, mas são unidades privadas, com as quais a prefeitura fez parcerias para abertura de vagas na rede pública.

O tema das creches conveniadas foi, aliás, debatido nas eleições de 2024, quando João Campos foi reeleito. Na época, a oposição apontou supostas irregularidades nesse modelo de abertura de vagas, e o assunto dominou boa parte do guia eleitoral da época e se transformou numa das principais polêmicas da campanha.

"A Guarda Municipal do Recife tem um efetivo maior do que a Polícia Civil de Pernambuco."

O efetivo da Guarda Municipal do Recife é 3,3 vezes menor que o de policiais civis do estado.

Segundo dados do Portal da Transparência da prefeitura, há, atualmente, 1.606 agentes de segurança municipal. Por outro lado, o efetivo atual de policiais civis em Pernambuco é de 5,3 mil, conforme afirmado pela Secretaria de Defesa Social ao Fato ou Fake .

Na gestão de João Campos, houve redução de mais de 300 agentes, já que, no início de seu primeiro mandato, a guarda tinha 1.955 agentes, ainda conforme os dados do Portal da Transparência.

Nos dois mandatos de João Campos como prefeito, não foi realizado nenhum concurso público para a guarda. A prefeitura anunciou a realização de uma seleção de 400 profissionais neste ano, já na gestão de Victor Marques (PCdoB). Porém, até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia sido publicado o edital nem o cronograma do certame.

Procurada pelo Fato ou Fake , a assessoria de imprensa de João Campos disse que o candidato quis estabelecer um paralelo "entre os quantitativos de servidores desses dois órgãos à disposição da capital pernambucana". A resposta cita que, com isso, haveria 1.539 servidores policiais civis das carreiras investigativas em unidades classificadas como de "atividade-fim" e sediadas na cidade.

"Tem uma pergunta que eu preciso fazer para o senhor [João Campos] em nome de uma mulher que foi agredida por Fábio Tyrone em 2018. O nome dela se chama Miriam Gadelha. Ela foi espancada por ele. Ele é réu confesso e foi julgado e condenado pela Justiça. E hoje é candidato a deputado federal pelo seu partido."

O ex-prefeito de Sousa (PB) e candidato a deputado federal Fábio Tyrone foi condenado a um ano e quatro meses de prisão em 18 de maio de 2023 , por agredir com tapas, chutes e soco a então namorada, a advogada Myriam Gadelha, em dezembro de 2018.

Um exame de corpo de delito identificou marcas de agressões no rosto, pescoço, região lombar e perna da vítima. Também foram localizadas marcas de sangue dentro do apartamento.

A pena foi reduzida para 10 meses e 25 dias em abril deste ano, pelo ministro Messod Azulay Neto, do Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ).

Também em abril, a deputada federal Tabata Amaral (PSB), esposa de João Campos, pediu a expulsão de Tyrone do partido. Antes disso, em 2023, o PSB Mulher pediu à Executiva Nacional a expulsão.

No debate, João Campos disse "há alguns dias eu já determinei a expulsão dele do PSB" e afirmou que o Conselho de Ética do partido vai retirá-lo da lista de filiados.

"Mas você, como prefeito do Recife, colocou a Guarda Municipal sem concurso público no pior momento da sua história, no abandono, sem concurso e sem investimento."

Embora o efetivo da Guarda Municipal tenha reduzido nas gestões de João Campos, a prefeitura anunciou, em fevereiro, a realização de um concurso público para contratação de 400 agentes. O certame ainda não tem previsão para ser aberto, mas, em setembro, uma banca organizadora foi contratada para a realização.

Além disso, em março, a prefeitura anunciou um pacote de medidas para o efetivo, com novos equipamentos, veículos, aplicativo que permite a gestão e o monitoramento da atuação dos agentes no território e contêiner de videomonitoramento no Bairro do Recife.

Outra mudança na Guarda Municipal foi o armamento de parte do efetivo. Em março de 2026, uma primeira turma de agentes foi treinada para usar o equipamento e começou a atuar com pistolas. Os agentes também usam câmeras corporais.

"Quando foi prefeito, ele [João Campos] mandou uma lei reduzindo de 5% para 2% imposto sobre bets [...] e disse o seguinte, entre aspas, na justificativa do projeto: 'É salutar que casas de apostas se instalem aqui para alavancar o município do Recife como polo sede para estas empresas'. Isso foi antes da regulamentação do presidente Lula, que fez sobre bets."

João Campos sancionou uma alteração no Código Tributário do Recife que reduziu o imposto para bets de 5% para 2% a alíquota do Imposto sobre Serviços (ISS) para serviços de jogos, loterias e sorteios. Também enviou um ofício à Câmara Municipal sugerindo tornar a cidade “mais competitiva” para essas empresas.

Entretanto, o projeto só foi enviado para a Câmara de Vereadores em 14 de março de 2025, ao passo que a regulamentação do mercado de apostas foi sancionada pelo presidente Lula (PT) em dezembro de 2023 , portanto, antes da lei das bets no Recife.

No período da tarde, ele concedeu entrevista para uma emissora de TV.

À noite, o candidato finalizou os compromissos do dia em uma reunião com apoiadores na Zona Leste de Porto Velho (RO).

Pela manhã, o candidato realizou uma caminhada com apoiadores na Zona Sul de Porto Velho (RO). Em seguida, participou de uma reunião com lideranças e concedeu entrevista a um canal de rádio.

No período da tarde, ele se reuniu com lideranças na Zona Leste de Porto Velho (RO).

articles.title: Coronel Busnello propõe reduzir secretarias e cargos no RJ | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do Missão fez uma caminhada pelo Centro de Petrópolis, na Região Serrana, nesta quarta-feira (30).
articles.summary: Em caminhada por Petrópolis, o candidato Coronel Busnello detalhou planos para reduzir gastos públicos, auditar contratos e implementar o prontuário único na saúde fluminense.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Rio de Janeiro Coronel Busnello (Missão) fez uma caminhada pelo Centro de Petrópolis, na Região Serrana, nesta quarta-feira (30).

O candidato afirmou que, se for eleito governador, pretende reduzir o número de secretarias e de cargos em comissão para reduzir o gasto público.

Outra proposta de Busnello é auditar e revisar os contratos do estado. Na saúde, o candidato defendeu a adoção de um prontuário único, com o histórico dos pacientes.

Segundo ele, a medida evitaria a repetição de consultas e exames, e ajudaria a otimizar os recursos do SUS.

Para a Região Serrana, o candidato afirmou ser importante a integração entre a Defesa Civil do estado e os municípios, para identificar áreas de risco e atender a população em situações de perigo.

articles.title: Norway launches probe into 11 senior officials over US Epstein files links
articles.summary: Norway investigates over $13m in state grants linked to Epstein and top ministers.
articles.body:
Norway’s Parliament has launched an investigation into 11 current and former high-ranking ministers — including Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere — over alleged ties and grants linked to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

US President Donald Trump’s Department of Justice in January released millions of Epstein-related documents, revealing connections to politicians, royals and the ultra-rich around the world.

Norway, home of the Nobel Peace Prize and often a fulcrum of international diplomacy, has seen major fallout, triggering parliamentary inquiries and police investigations.

The public hearing, which began on Wednesday, comes in light of reports that the Foreign Ministry allocated over 130 million kroner ($13.5m) to the International Peace Institute between 1997 and 2018.

The United Nations-affiliated think-tank was led by Terje Rod-Larsen, a prominent Norwegian diplomat and chief architect of the 1993 Oslo Accords, from 2005 to 2020. Stoere, who has denied any wrongdoing, served as foreign minister from 2005 to 2012.

A central figure in the Middle East peace talks in the 1990s, Rod-Larsen was implicated in the files and Norwegian media investigations that exposed an alleged relationship involving illicit loans and visa fraud for sex-trafficked women. Epstein also left Rod-Larsen’s children millions of dollars in his will.

The government must explain what it is doing to restore trust in the foreign service, said Jonas Andersen Sayed, who chaired the hearing at Parliament’s Committee on Scrutiny and Constitutional Affairs.

“There are many people who have demonstrated very poor judgement,” Andersen Sayed told the Reuters news agency in reference to friends of Epstein.

While testifying, the prime minister maintained that he had never had any relationship with Epstein and said the “problems” were isolated lapses, not systemic to the Foreign Ministry.

“There is no reason to speak of an unhealthy culture at a large organisation just because of what one or several people may have done,” Stoere told the committee.

Stoere added that, to his knowledge, Epstein wielded no influence over Norway’s foreign policy, development aid or any other government decisions.

Erik Solheim, a former development minister who will testify on Wednesday, has said parliament’s probe is an overreaction that will throttle the foreign service as diplomats opt for needless self-restraint, harming the national interest.

Though not appearing before Parliament, a number of other prominent Norwegians with ties to Epstein — including former premier Thorbjoern Jagland, Roed-Larsen and his wife, ex-diplomat Mona Juul — are under police investigation on corruption accusations.

“The Epstein documents raise serious questions about abuse of office, a culture of accountability failures and poor management of development aid funds,” said Andersen Sayed.

“The issue concerns public trust in the entire system. It is essential that all the facts are brought to light, that accountability is established and that the necessary reforms are implemented,” he said.

Parliament has also set up an independent inquiry tasked with a much broader examination of the case, which is due to submit its final report by January 31, 2028.

articles.title: Flydubai FZ1073 timeline: How the Israel-bound flight emergency unfolded
articles.summary: Flydubai flight diverts to Saudi Arabia after cockpit emergency, as Netanyahu alleges a crash attempt.
articles.body:
A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia on Wednesday after issuing emergency signals.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later said one pilot stabbed the other and tried to crash the aircraft. There has been no independent confirmation of a hijacking attempt.

The co-pilot, whom an Israeli official identified as an Omani national, was arrested after the plane landed, Netanyahu said. Israel’s Ministry of Transport said there would be a joint investigation of the incident with the defence establishment. The nationality of the arrested individual has not been independently verified.

The emergency came a day after Netanyahu warned of possible attacks in the run-up to Israel’s October 27 election . Here is how events unfolded:

September 29: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel has indications that its “enemies” could try to carry out attacks before the October 27 election. He does not specify the nature of the threat.

Later that night at about 20:30 GMT , opposition leader Yair Lapid receives a security briefing from Netanyahu. After the meeting, Lapid says there is “no reason to put the public in a panic” and says that security threats should be handled professionally rather than used in election messaging.

September 30 at 03:05 GMT: Flydubai flight FZ1073 departs Dubai for Tel Aviv, climbing to 34,000 feet (more than 10,000 metres), according to Flightradar24 .

05:21 GMT: Flightradar24 data shows that the aircraft starts with a deep descent, is then followed by a sharp climb and a second steep descent. By about 05:33 GMT , it is flying at roughly 15,000 feet (4,572 metres).

05:28 GMT: The aircraft begins transmitting the emergency transponder code 7700, the internationally agreed-upon code for a general emergency, as it is flying near the border between Saudi Arabia and Jordan.

05:35 GMT: The transponder changes to 7500, signalling unlawful interference; after that, the aircraft turns west, briefly enters Jordanian airspace and then turns back towards Saudi Arabia.

05:44 GMT: Air traffic controllers in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia get a distress call from FZ1073 asking for an emergency landing. Saudi authorities give the time as 08:44 local time.

As the aircraft approaches Tabuk, its transponder switches back to 7700, indicating a general emergency.

06:45 GMT: According to local media , the plane FZ1073 lands safely at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk.

Flightradar24 receives the aircraft’s final tracking signal at 06:58GMT at Tabuk airport.

Flydubai said the flight experienced an “incident” and was diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely, adding that all passengers were safe and accounted for. The UAE has not publicly commented on the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Later on September 30, Netanyahu said in a video message that the co-pilot stabbed the pilot and apparently attempted to crash the plane.

He added that passengers and a crew member entered the cockpit and restrained the co-pilot. It is not clear what the exact time was when Netanyahu recorded or released the video.

Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid rejects attempts to connect the Flydubai incident to a security briefing he received from Netanyahu.

“Let me make this clear. Nothing even resembling this morning’s plane incident appeared in the security briefing with the prime minister last night. Nothing similar, nothing reminiscent of it, not even a hint,” he said on X.

Lapid accused government-aligned voices of trying to use the incident for political purposes.

Later that afternoon, footage from international news agencies showed a Flydubai rescue flight, carrying passengers from FZ1073, arriving at Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv at 15:34 GMT .

articles.title: French court sentences 13 men over deadliest small-boat crossing to UK
articles.summary: Six people smugglers are found guilty of involuntary homicide after 31 migrants died in the English Channel in 2021.
articles.body:
A French court has sentenced 13 men to up to 10 years in prison for their roles in the deadliest small-boat crossing by migrants trying to reach the United Kingdom from France.

The court in Paris found six of the men guilty of involuntary homicide on Wednesday, handing down prison terms of between six and 10 years. Prosecutors said they organised the crossing of a small boat that was unfit for navigation on the open sea, was overloaded with 31 passengers and lacked appropriate life jackets.

The remaining seven men were found guilty of lesser criminal charges and were sentenced to up to four years in jail. There were 14 defendants on trial, one of whom was acquitted.

The court said the smugglers were driven by greed and were “profiting from the vulnerability of exile candidates”.

“When it costs the lives of 31 people and the sea becomes a cemetery, there is a price, and the court said that the price they had to pay was justice and prison time,” said Emmanuel Daoud, a lawyer for victims’ families.

The migrants, mostly Iraqi Kurds, drowned after the UK-bound small boat carrying them from northern France capsized in the English Channel in November 2021. Four of the bodies were never found, while two men survived.

Seven military personnel are still being investigated for allegedly failing to help the survivors. They all deny any wrongdoing.

The sentencing of the 13 men comes as France and the UK end their pilot scheme that allowed Britain to return migrants from France deemed not to have the legal right to remain in the country.

In return, the UK accepted an equivalent number of migrants whose asylum claims were likely to be granted.

The scheme was due to expire on Thursday. However, unverified reports say the UK government wanted the programme to continue.

The UK Interior Ministry confirmed earlier on Wednesday that new applications were no longer being accepted.

articles.title: Displaced by war, young Sudanese turn to entrepeneurship to survive
articles.summary: Displaced by war and shut out of formal jobs, young Sudanese are turning to art, small businesses, and entrepeneurship.
articles.body:
Yousra Hussein’s career was on the rise. She had graduated with a degree in medical laboratory sciences from Nahda College in 2022, and then began developing a women’s empowerment initiative – Golden Women – in the western Sudanese city of Nyala, in the same year.

The initiative organised psychosocial support sessions and training workshops in marketing and entrepreneurship that helped more than 70 women. Yousra wanted to help young women like her seeking work, but often lacking the experience and practical skills needed to pursue available opportunities.

Things were going well until Sudan’s civil war began in April 2023 , upending her life. By June, Yousra and her family fled Nyala to Sennar, a city in central Sudan that she had never visited.

“Before the war, I was ambitious and had many dreams,” Yousra told Al Jazeera. “I started from zero in Sennar, without work experience or connections.”

Unable to find work in a city that she was unfamiliar with, she began offering nail services from home, charging the equivalent of about $10 to $15, and saving what she could to help her family.

Then, fighting between the two belligerents in Sudan’s war – the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces – spread to Sennar in mid-2024 , forcing Yousra and her family to flee once again, this time to Kassala in eastern Sudan.

Once again, Yousra was starting from scratch, and Sudan’s economy was collapsing as a result of the war. With few jobs available, and the growing need Yousra saw for women to earn money to support their families, she has resurrected her Golden Women initiative.

But while she has been able to raise some income through the initiative, funding remains a major obstacle. Yousra said young Sudanese entrepreneurs have limited access to skills training and institutional support, as well as struggling with bank requirements for guarantees that many cannot provide. She also pointed to complex registration procedures and taxes as barriers to establishing and sustaining a business.

Yousra’s experiences reflect a wider collapse in jobs and livelihoods.

In a 2024 joint report by the United Nations Development Fund and the International Food Policy Research Institute, 31 percent of the 3,000 urban households surveyed had been displaced, while the share reporting no employment or income rose from 1.6 percent before the war to about 18 percent by the time of the survey. Full-time employment also fell by half.

The World Bank, meanwhile, estimates that even as the economy grew modestly last year, with the government attempting to stabilise the areas of Sudan under its control, the percentage of the population living in extreme poverty rose from 33 percent in 2022 to 59 percent in 2025.

For young people whose education and livelihoods have been disrupted, the shrinking labour market has pushed some towards entrepreneurship and informal work as they search for ways to support themselves and their families, but they may not have the skills or experience to go into business for themselves.

International and government-backed programmes have been initiated to help some Sudanese develop the skills that they’ll need to run businesses.

The International Labour Organization said in May that its i-UPSHIFT programme had reached 500 young people in Kassala, providing entrepreneurship training, mentorship, and business incubation. Thirty-eight youth-led teams – involving 160 participants, including 66 internally displaced people – went on to pitch business and social-enterprise ideas.

Sudan’s Ministry of Youth and Sports says it has also promoted vocational training and youth-led projects. Minister Ahmed Adam Ahmed told Al Jazeera that two youth conferences had been held in Atbara and Kassala in an attempt to understand the views and aspirations of young people, as part of an effort to equip young people with practical skills that could help them earn an income.

Ahmed explained that one of the first conference’s outcomes was a proposed industrial city in River Nile State intended to support youth-led enterprises.

“Projects were also directed towards implementation in states considered safe, with some already under way,” Ahmed said. “The second conference in Kassala focused on practical applications and innovation, particularly artificial intelligence and the use of agricultural waste.”

The struggle to earn a living after displacement affects many Sudanese. Mahira, a 30-year-old visual artist who did not wish to give her full name, moved to Port Sudan after her home in Khartoum was damaged during the war.

She now paints decorative pieces and murals, earning about 1 million Sudanese pounds ($130 at parallel market exchange rates) to help support her husband and son, but has worked a variety of jobs since being displaced.

Before the war, she graduated with a degree in French and completed a diploma in fine arts, both from Sudan University of Science and Technology.

“Since the war began, my main concern has been finding any income , no matter how much, to meet my family’s daily needs, despite how difficult it has been to find opportunities and funding,” she told Al Jazeera.

Mahira initially took on several jobs in Port Sudan, including making soap, applying henna and makeup, and styling clothes. She then began working in home decoration after she volunteered to paint the walls of a woman’s house in the Salbouna neighbourhood.

“Everyone was surprised by my skills in decorating and beautifying homes,” she said. “After that, requests started coming from other residents in the neighbourhood asking me to paint and decorate their homes.”

She later turned to more of her artistic work, conducting workshops on concrete art – an art form that uses cement-based materials to create decorative and artistic pieces – and teaching traditional dance at shelters. She worked with nongovernmental organisations running psychosocial support and skills-training programmes for displaced people.

Mahira now hopes to stage an exhibition featuring paintings that challenge hate speech and promote peaceful coexistence, while also giving her a way to market her work and build a more sustainable income.

At the same time, the exhibition would cost at least 8 million Sudanese pounds ($1,000), but Mahira says she has no savings and earns only about 1 million pounds per month. And yet, Mahira is still optimistic that she can raise the funds, and believes in the benefits the exhibition will bring – not just to herself.

“We need to promote peace and peaceful coexistence in Sudan, because the war has affected society and fuelled hate speech based on ethnic and tribal identity,” she told Al Jazeera.

articles.title: Two dead in Canada after vehicle hits pedestrians taking part in First Nations event
articles.summary: Police said the driver "may have been experiencing a medical emergency" before hitting four people in British Columbia.
articles.body:
Two people were killed and two others were injured after a vehicle hit pedestrians during a community walk marking Canada's National Day for Truth and Reconciliation in British Columbia.

The incident occurred on Tsawwassen First Nation land, south of Vancouver near the US-Canada border.

Police said the driver "may have been experiencing a medical emergency" before the collision, and that there is no ongoing risk to public safety.

They added they do not believe it is related to Truth and Reconciliation day, a national holiday that honours victims and survivors of Canada's residential schools, which sought to forcefully assimilate indigenous children.

The collision happened at around 10:25 local time (16:25 BST) at a local parking lot, said the Delta Police Department, which covers the area where the incident occurred.

Police said they are at the scene investigating and have advised residents to avoid the area. They added that the two injured are receiving treatment in hospital.

"Our thoughts are with the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this tragic incident," Delta Police said.

Eyewitness accounts by CBC News reporters on scene say more than a dozen ambulances were responding to the incident.

In a social media post advertising the event last week, Tsawwassen First Nation said it had planned a community walk followed by the unveiling of a house post in honour of the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.

The event was due to take place from 09:30 to 13:00 local time.

In an X post that now appears to be deleted, Canada's energy minister Tim Hodgson said he attended the walk and posted two images from the event.

A spokesperson for the minister, Carolyn Svonkin, said he was not near the incident when it occurred.

Tsawwassen First Nation is home to 491 members, according to its website, with half living on Tsawwassen lands and others in nearby areas, including across the border in Bellingham, Washington.

Canada began observing its National Day for Truth and Reconciliation in 2021, following news of the discovery of unmarked burial sites at former residential schools.

The holiday coincides with Orange Shirt Day - an indigenous grassroots-led day of remembrance to honour children who were missing or died in residential schools.

articles.title: Northumberland’s ‘Lady of the North’ captured in new drone images as the world’s largest female-form land sculpture, rising 100 feet and built from 1.5 million tonnes of rock and soil from the former Shotton Surface Mine
articles.summary: New drone images have captured the scale of the “Lady of the North”, a vast land sculpture in Northumberland that is recognised as the world’s largest
articles.body: New drone images have captured the scale of the “Lady of the North”, a vast land sculpture in Northumberland that is recognised as the world’s largest land sculpture of the female form. Spanning around a quarter of a mile and rising more than 100 feet, the artwork transforms a former mining landscape into a striking living landmark.Known as the “Lady of the North”, the sculpture depicts a reclining female figure and was created using around 1.5 million tonnes of rock and soil left behind by the now-defunct Shotton Surface Mine in Northumberland.The project was conceived by artist Charles Jencks, with plans beginning in 2004. Construction was completed in 2010.Rather than remaining a static monument, the sculpture was designed as a “living landscape”. Hydro-seed was planted across the landform, allowing vegetation to develop and change with the seasons.Landform requires annual maintenanceDespite its enormous size, the sculpture requires regular maintenance to preserve its distinctive shape.Local landscaper Stephen Coatsworth has been responsible for cutting the landform since 2012. The annual task takes around a week and involves a combination of large and smaller machinery.“We cut it with a big machine, which takes about three days, then we come in with smaller machines for the steeper areas,” Coatsworth said, according to SWNS.The most challenging sections are around the face of the sculpture, where some parts of the landform are almost vertical.“Up by the face is a really steep area – some of that has to be done with a hedge cutter because it’s nearly vertical,” he said.Team tackles steep sections by handCoatsworth typically works with a team of between three and five employees to maintain the sculpture.The team begins with larger machinery before moving to smaller equipment for the more difficult sections.“It takes about a week – but I like to see how much I can get done with the big machine and then work out from there,” Coatsworth said.While he has years of experience maintaining the giant landform, working on its steep slopes can still be daunting.“It can sometimes be a bit scary, but I’m getting used to it now,” he said.“It’s a lovely job to be doing – but I’m quite glad to get home safely every night.”A changing landscapeThe annual cutting ensures that the contours of the reclining figure remain visible while allowing the surrounding vegetation to develop naturally.Since its completion in 2010, the “Lady of the North” has become an example of how former industrial land can be transformed into a large-scale artwork and evolving landscape.The drone images provide a striking view of the sculpture’s full form, showing how the vast female figure sits within the Northumberland countryside.You use AI every day. articles.title: US judge rules Wisconsin mosque leader Salah Sarsour can be deported
articles.summary: Sarsour’s lawyers say the decision threatens free speech protections and plan to fight the ruling.
articles.body:
A United States immigration judge has ruled the leader of Wisconsin’s largest mosque can be deported under a controversial law that United States President Donald Trump’s administration has used against non-citizens advocating for Palestinian rights.

Judge Jayme Salinardi ruled on Wednesday that Palestinian-born Salah Sarsour, president of the Islamic Society of Milwaukee, can be removed from the US based in part on a memo by Secretary of State Marco Rubio that “his actions undermine US foreign policy to combat antisemitism around the world”, according to his lawyers.

Sarsour, who has lived in the US for more than three decades, called the ruling “deeply disappointing”.

“I will continue fighting to defend the right to free speech and to stay in the country I have called home for more than three decades,” he told The Associated Press news agency.

His lawyer, Patrick Taurel, strongly rejected the decision.

“I wish the world could see the evidence that we presented and hear the testimony that the court heard because the case we presented compels only one conclusion, which is that Salah is not deportable,” Taurel told reporters on Wednesday.

“He’s done nothing wrong. He should be given back his green card, frankly, with an apology for what’s being done to him.”

The ruling does not mean Sarsour will be immediately deported.

His lawyers have 60 days to argue that sending Sarsour back would put him at risk of torture, which could protect him from deportation under the Convention Against Torture. If they lose, they plan to appeal. Taurel said he can’t be deported while that appeal is pending and will remain in the US for the “foreseeable future”.

Sarsour was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers in Milwaukee in March, nine months after Rubio issued a memo declaring him deportable on foreign policy grounds.

The June 2025 memo invoked a rarely-used US law that allows the Secretary of State to seek the deportation of non-citizens whose presence could have “potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences.” The administration has used the same provision against pro-Palestinian activists Mahmoud Khalil and Mohsen Mahdawi.

Sarsour’s lawyers criticised the “extreme deference” Salinardi gave to Rubio’s memo. But Taurel said the judge believed his hands were tied by an earlier ruling in Khalil’s case, which found that a letter from the Secretary of State could be enough to make someone deportable on foreign policy grounds.

That meant Salinardi could not look behind Rubio’s decision to examine the evidence supporting it, Taurel said.

“If the Secretary of State says the person is deportable, it is game over,” he told reporters Wednesday.

The government did not win on all of its arguments.

Salinardi rejected its allegation that Sarsour had lied on his green card application. Taurel said the judge also rejected an allegation that Sarsour had falsely claimed to be a US citizen in order to vote.

Al Jazeera reached out to the State Department and the Department of Homeland Security but did not receive responses by the time of publication.

Sarsour is separately fighting the Trump administration in federal court over his detention while his deportation case is ongoing.

A federal judge ordered his release from ICE custody in June after 81 days, questioning why decades-old convictions that US authorities had long known about suddenly justified detaining him. The judge found there was a “substantial” case that the government was retaliating against him for speaking out about Palestinian rights.

The Trump administration has appealed his release, arguing that Sarsour’s convictions in Israel make him a security threat. He was imprisoned in 1988 after confessing to throwing stones and a Molotov cocktail at Israeli military personnel, and was convicted again in 1995 over an attempt to hold weapons.

Sarsour denies the offences, and his lawyers say the confessions were forced through torture. His former lawyer, Jawad Boulos, testified in August that Sarsour was coerced into signing confessions and was not convicted of an offence tying him to a “terrorist” organisation.

Taurel criticised Salinardi for giving what he called “extreme deference” to Israeli government records submitted by ICE, which Sarsour’s lawyers argue were incomplete and relied on confessions obtained through torture.

“A great deal of evidence we presented was ignored,” Taurel said.

The evidence challenged Israel’s military court system, where he said secret evidence can be used and Palestinians can be denied access to lawyers for extended periods.

Luna Droubi, an attorney representing Sarsour, said the case raises broader questions about whether immigrants can speak freely on political issues without fear of being targeted by the government.

“Why raise these arrests now?” she said. “Do I have the right to speak out about issues that matter to me? What if I draw a political cartoon? Am I going to be arrested and detained because of that?”

Sarsour said being deported to the occupied West Bank “means the end of my life”.

His lawyers argue his prior treatment in Israeli custody shows he could face torture if sent back. Taurel said Sarsour’s former lawyer testified that his case stood out because Sarsour told him that Shin Bet, Israel’s internal security agency, had taken him to hospital while in custody.

The judge also named Jordan as a possible destination. Sarsour travelled to the US on a Jordanian-issued document, but his lawyers say he is not a Jordanian citizen and has no right to live there. They believe he could ultimately be returned to the West Bank and Israeli custody if sent to Jordan.

articles.title: Every product our shopping experts tested and loved enough to buy in September: Calpak, Hommey and more
articles.summary: This month, we tried out lots of products like toner pads, wireless earbuds, robes, cordless vacuums and more.
articles.body: For me, and likely a lot of other people, September ended up being my busiest month so far this year. When summer ends, it feels like you have to tend to every responsibility, obligation and errand all at the same time. Not to mention, people are going back to school, football season comes back (which means there are more events to attend) and fall weather calls for wardrobe reset. In the end, though, we at NBC Selected always make time to test products, some of which we include in roundups, shopping guides and product reviews. Below, my colleagues and I highlighted tons of products we tested and purchased this month because we loved them so much — including ones from our favorite brands like Levoit, Medicube, Calpak, Hommey and more. The best products we tried in September 2026 All of the products below were either sent courtesy of the brand for testing or products that we bought ourselves. Jem Alabi, editorial operations associate I received the VortexIQ from Levoit for testing and it has become my go-to vacuum, and I’d argue it works just as well as, if not better than, my cordless Dyson. It’s lightweight, stands upright on its own and works equally well on my rugs and hardwood floors. My favorite feature is the LED green light, which is incredibly bright and makes dust, hair and debris I would otherwise miss much easier to see, especially along edges and in crevices. It also has a five-stage HEPA filtration system, a 210-watt motor and an anti-tangle roller designed to prevent hair from wrapping around the brush. On a full charge, I can get nearly an hour of cleaning time. I originally took this duffel as my carry-on for an international trip, but I liked it so much that it has since replaced my everyday work bag. The vegan leather feels incredibly soft, and the padded handles and adjustable strap are comfortable on my sensitive shoulders, even when I pack it full. I chose the dark cherry color, which has a rich, distinctive look that makes the bag feel more elevated than your typical travel duffel. It has nine pockets, including a separate shoe compartment, plus a luggage sleeve and a spacious main compartment that somehow fits just about everything I need while still zipping closed easily. It’s also designed to fit underneath most airplane seats, which made it particularly convenient as a carry-on. I also have the Luka Crescent Bag which is a smaller crossbody that I use to carry my travel documents, lip balms, hand sanitizer and other small essentials. I received this bag at a Calpak press event. This is pretty much my ideal bonnet size, especially since I have a lot of hair to fit inside, and I wear it every night. Before bed, I’ll usually add a little water and mousse to my hair, put the bonnet on and wake up with my hair looking noticeably more polished and manageable. The satin helps retain moisture and natural oils while reducing tangles, and the oversized design works particularly well for long or curly hair. I also like the extra-long adjustable ties, which help keep it securely in place overnight without feeling restrictive. The cherry print is cute enough that I don’t mind wearing it around the house, either. These may be the most versatile sunglasses I own. I wore them with a formal dress to an outdoor birthday party on a hot summer day. The pillow-shaped frames have dark green lenses and a polished finish that gives them a sleek, slightly edgy look without feeling overly trendy. They also work especially well for my low nose bridge. Unlike a lot of sunglasses I’ve tried, these stayed in place and didn’t constantly slide down my nose, and the frames didn’t press into or leave indents on my cheeks. I love a purple blush, and this YSL in Spicy Berry is one of the few I’ve tried that actually looks like a true purple rather than turning pink once I apply it. The formula is pigmented but buildable, so I can use a light hand for a subtle wash of color or layer it when I want the purple to really stand out. It’s also waterproof and lasts on me throughout the day without needing frequent touch-ups. The powder contains squalane and rosehip oil and is designed to blur the appearance of pores and imperfections while leaving either a matte or satin finish, depending on the shade. Plus, the YSL compact is beautiful enough that I actually enjoy pulling it out of my makeup bag. I bought this at an airport duty-free shop, which was actually my first-ever duty-free fragrance purchase, after being immediately drawn to how fresh it smelled. I especially like that it’s gender-neutral and blends nicely with my natural scent rather than overpowering it. I’m conscious of wearing strong fragrances around coworkers and people who may be sensitive to perfume, so I appreciate that this one doesn’t feel heavy or linger aggressively on my clothes. This might be a controversial fragrance opinion, but I also like that it doesn’t last forever too. I can wear a subtle amount during the day and add another spritz later if I want to refresh it rather than committing to an intense scent for several hours. I get so many compliments on this phone case, but the wristlet is what makes it particularly useful for me. I commute on the train regularly, and being able to loop it securely around my wrist gives me a little extra peace of mind when I’m holding my phone in a crowded car or station. The sculptural design combines glossy and chrome finishes, so it’s distinctive enough that I can also spot my phone much more quickly when it’s buried in my bag or sitting somewhere in my apartment. It feels more like an accessory than a standard phone case. I received this case from the brand. None of the closets in my apartment have built-in lighting, so for years I used my phone flashlight whenever I needed to find clothes or supplies. My friend Jasmine, who is a professional organizer, recommended these rechargeable lights, and they’ve made a surprisingly big difference. I chose the version with three color temperatures, including white, warm and natural light, plus five brightness levels. I primarily use the automatic motion-sensor setting, and in my experience, a single charge lasts around three weeks. They attach magnetically, so installation was simple, and I can easily pull them off the wall when they need to be recharged with a USB cable. The brand says a full charge can last between seven and 45 days in motion-sensor mode depending on usage. I bought two of these racks to hang coats and towels, and I like that their simple design blends easily with the rest of my decor. The one-inch-diameter hooks are substantial enough that I can hang bulky coats, bags and even towels without loops without worrying about them constantly slipping onto the floor. The rack has rounded edges and a smooth, satin-lacquered finish, which also helps prevent the hooks from snagging or damaging clothing. Each rack has a recommended maximum load of 40 pounds and comes with mounting hardware for both drywall and brick, making it a practical option for heavier everyday items. Cory Fernandez, commerce editor We’ve written a lot about all of Medicube’s many viral skin care products, and these pore pads are by far one of the brand’s most popular. I don’t expect many toner pads like this to make much of a visible difference in my skin, but since they’re so highly reviewed I decided to try them out. While it’s only been a few weeks, I’d say they’ve been working well for me and even helped get rid of some hyperpigmentation I had on my nose. They don’t burn or irritate my skin and they also don’t cause my seborrheic dermatitis to flare up, which is a common problem for me. Overall, I’d say that if anyone is wondering if these are worth it, they should definitely try them. Marilyn La Jeunesse, freelance newsletter editor There’s nothing I love more than matching my candles to the seasons, and the Voluspa x Fender collaboration candle has been the perfect choice for this year’s fall pick. I received a sample to try it and, although I was hesitant about liking a leather-scented candle, I found the scent to be perfectly balanced with warm spices like ginger and cardamom and the faintest hint of incense. It feels somehow both peaceful and intriguing whenever I light it in my office. Plus, I love how chic the vessel looks on my bookshelf. As an avid reader who brings physical books almost everywhere, I am constantly losing my bookmarks. In an effort to stop folding the edges of my books, I tested a sample of these magnetic bookmarks from Galison. Not only do I love how cute and nostalgic the Miffy design is, I was surprised at how sturdy they are when placed inside a book. The last time I used magnetic bookmarks, the tops of my pages ripped, but I haven’t had that problem with these after a few weeks of use. Needless to say, I’m impressed (and probably not going to lose these any time soon, especially with how cute they are). Pumpkin spice lattes are great, but I wanted to switch things up this year with Diaspora Co. Black Pepper Ginger Syrup. I received a sample from the brand and instantly fell in love with how warm and spicy this is in my morning lattes. I add 2 ounces of espresso, a tablespoon of this syrup (which goes in and out of stock pretty frequently), about 6 ounces of steamed oat milk and top it with Diaspora Gingerbread Spice for an extra hit of flavor. Not only is it the perfect fall drink, each bottle makes about 25 coffees. It beats paying $8 a day for a seasonal beverage in the city, in my opinion. I love hosting and recently received a gift box filled with tons of Dylan’s Candy Bar Halloween treats ahead of my Books and Boos party this year. While I’m normally really good at waiting to break into my Halloween candy, I couldn’t resist opening one of the gummy kebobs, which features skewered gummy spiders, skulls and vampire fangs. I really appreciated the balance of sweet and sour options on this seasonal treat, and I think these will make the cutest addition to any boo basket. Shalwah Evans, senior editor I had the pleasure of testing the AirPods 5 right before they were released and I was thoroughly impressed. I rarely update my devices if they’re not broken or low-functioning, but my first thought when I used these was that I needed to get a pair (which I got from Apple) — and that was before enabling active noise canceling. The sound of music and podcasts is excellent with and without ANC, but one of the biggest standouts for me is how well I can hear my surroundings in transparency mode. Now I can walk my dog with the buds on and switch modes quickly when we go from the park to crossing busy streets. They also sit comfortably in the ear for hours, which is a huge benefit for someone like me who travels a few times a year and swears by audiobooks on hours-long flights. Mili Godio, commerce editor My collection of robes has grown to more than a dozen over the years, but few have wowed me as much as this Hommey one. It’s one of the softest, coziest robes I’ve ever put on my body, and the one I reach for after every shower. Since it’s on the thicker side, I was initially afraid I would get too warm in it. But that wasn’t the case at all; in fact, it’s more breathable than many of the thinner robes I have in my stash. The chunky stripes and trendy colors make it even cooler; I’ve had multiple people ask me where I got it when they see it hanging in my bathroom. I recently moved into a new apartment and have been furnishing it with small spaces in mind. The brand sent me this stool to add as a side table in my living room, and it fits perfectly and adds so much flair without being too loud. So many side tables are just a little too big for a small city-living space, but this one manages to fit in any tiny spot I put it in. Right now, it’s decorated with a fall-inspired wreath for the new season. Earlier this month, I had a bachelorette trip to the Hamptons, where we did a Pilates class and wore matching butter yellow workout sets. I decided to go with Popflex’s Supershort and matching Corset Bra, and the compliments kept flooding in. I’m normally a leggings workout kind of girl, but these shorts might have completely changed my mind; they have built-in stretchy shorts on the inside, which makes doing squats or moving on a reformer so much easier (without showing too much skin). The outer layer is flowy and breathable, so it looks like shorts I can wear out and about, not just in a workout class. Nikki Brown, senior editor Shopping as a very short person is rarely straightforward. More often than not, I have to get a lot of my wardrobe tailored after purchasing, including some pieces branded as “petite.” You would think something as lowkey as pajamas would be easier to manage, but it’s just as frustrating, especially when it comes to matching sets (my favorite). I wasted no time accepting a courtesy sample of Smol pajamas, which are made with people my height in mind, specifically, anyone 5-foot-3 and under. Slipping them on after wearing my heels for hours felt heavenly — I was in so much pain that I would have gone home barefoot if I didn’t have them. The foldable flats are officially going in my bag every time I wear heels from now on. articles.title: 'Hero' pilot stabbed by other pilot on Israel-bound plane, Israeli PM says
articles.summary: Passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and safely landed the plane in Saudi Arabia.
articles.body:
A pilot has been arrested after he stabbed the other pilot on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv and "apparently tried to crash the plane", Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said.

Passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control of the Flydubai aircraft, landing it safely at an airport in Tabuk, northwestern Saudi Arabia, with more than 170 people on board.

The passengers, who were almost all Israeli, arrived later on Wednesday to Tel Aviv on a repatriation flight.

The stabbed pilot, named as Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar, has been taken to hospital but is reported to be in a stable condition. Netanyahu praised him as a "true hero" of "extraordinary bravery".

"Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster," Netanyahu wrote on X.

"He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals."

The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said Machchhar was in a stable condition in hospital.

No official motive for the incident has been given, but Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has called it an "attempted jihadist terror attack".

US President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu following the incident, saying it seemed as though the attacker was "perhaps a terrorist" or there were other reasons behind the attack.

Flydubai's flight FZ1073 took off from Dubai International Airport in the United Arab Emirates at 03:05 GMT (07:05 local time), en route to Ben-Gurion Airport in Israel.

Around two and a half hours into its journey, data from flight tracking website Flightrader24 reported a rapid descent over Saudi Arabia, dropping more than 17,000 feet (over 5,000m) in less than two minutes.

Minutes later, the plane signalled an emergency code - squawk 7700 - before switching it to a squawk 7500 code reporting a hijacking.

Around twenty minutes after these codes were signalled, the plane looped back into Saudi Arabia, where it later started its manual descent for landing.

Less than an hour later, the plane returned to squawk 7700.

Shortly after the incident, the Israeli and Saudi Arabian air forces dispatched fighter jets, while Netanyahu held urgent consultations.

Initial media reports suggested a fight had broken out between the aircraft's two pilots, causing the rapid descent and landing.

However, in the hours after the plane touched down in Tabuk, eyewitness accounts and a statement by Netanyahu confirmed one of the pilots had stabbed the other and, according to the Israeli prime minister, "apparently tried to crash" the aircraft.

He said an Israeli passenger told him "the plane went into a spin and began to descend" before the passenger and a crew member broke into the cockpit and overpowered the "pilot who had carried out the stabbing".

Two on-duty crew travelling on the flight were then able to land the plane safely, Flydubai said.

In an address on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu called the situation "a very serious security incident" and said Israeli security forces are "maintaining close contact with the relevant authorities to ensure the continued safety of the passengers".

Unlike Israel's defence minister, Netanyahu did not give a motive for the incident.

"I salute these heroes who demonstrated extraordinary resourcefulness and courage," he added. "They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster."

Flydubai said in a statement that "an altercation occurred in the flight deck" and the flight was "successfully secured by on-duty Flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk airport".

An airline spokesperson added: "Our immediate priority is to ensure the ongoing safety, health, and wellbeing of all passengers and crew members involved in this incident and support the official investigation."

The passengers who had been on board flight FZ1073 arrived in Tel Aviv at around 18:40 local time (15:40 GMT). They were greeted at the airport by crowds of onlookers playing music, singing, dancing and waving Israeli flags.

A number of people were "very emotional and crying as they came off the plane," a paramedic from Israel's ambulance service told the BBC.

One passenger, Yaniv Hayun, met Netanyahu and told him how he and others on the flight had restrained the attacker.

"The pilot who was stabbed was simply very close to the door, so it was hard for us to open it," Hayun said in a video posted on social media by the prime minister's office, but before the stabbed pilot - now identified as Machchhar - collapsed, he was able to open the door.

Yaniv said he put the attacker, who was trying to disable the plane, in a chokehold before other passengers helped pin him down.

He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane and after it levelled out, another pilot took over control.

Zvika Meness, another passenger, told Israeli public broadcaster Kan News that he and other passengers tied the attacker up "with his own zip ties and with the multimedia headphones".

He said that: "There are children and families here who have been through a very severe, highly traumatic event."

articles.title: Anne Hathaway Skipped ‘Hot Ones’ Spicy Wings To Avoid Inducing Labor. Is That Even a Thing?
articles.summary: After actor Anne Hathaway, who’s expecting her third child, recently revealed that she skipped a “Hot Ones” interview for fear of inducing labor, many are wondering if there’s any truth to the concern.
articles.body: After actor Anne Hathaway, who’s expecting her third child, recently revealed that she skipped a “Hot Ones” interview for fear of inducing labor, many are wondering if there’s any truth to the concern. The “Verity” star recently spoke to podcast “Talk of the Townsends” and shared that her doctor advised against going on the popular spicy chicken wing challenge show because she “might go into early labor.” The comments echo a commonly circulated old wives’ tale — that having a couple piquant bites can kickstart the birthing process. But experts say that that’s not quite rooted in fact. “A lot of people coming to us … they all have this idea that one of the ways to start the induction process or to induce labor is to consume something hot, spicy,” says Francesco Callipari, medical director of the Carolyn Rowan Center for Women’s Health and Wellness at Mount Sinai in New York City. “There really is no evidence at all to support this.” “Hot Ones” features a challenge component in which the celebrity guest eats chicken wings between questions. Each wing features an increasingly spicier hot sauce. Hathaway has a similar scene in her new film, and explained during the podcast that she had planned to appear on the interview show to promote the movie. But her pregnancy caused her to pivot. Hathaway added during a Sept. 29 interview with E! News that “spicy foods impacted me in the past.” “So it kind of seemed like the right thing to do,” Hathaway told the outlet. “Why take any unnecessary chances?” Does Spicy Food Induce Labor? Callipari said that there are no randomized control trials, observational studies or otherwise to support the idea that spicy foods can induce labor. “Forget about causation,” he says. “There’s not even a correlation.” But it’s not entirely surprising that people believe these issues are linked. Callipari explains that hot foods tend to cause hypermotility of the gut, meaning that intestinal contractions increase and move the food faster. So some people experience gastrointestinal distress, prompting them to deal with loose bowel movements, he says. “Because the uterus is probably right next to the intestines and the colon and the abdomen, people think that this mechanistically may have an effect,” he says. Dr. Meleen Chuang, chief of obstetrics at NYU Langone Health, similarly says that there’s no compelling evidence to suggest a link between spice and an induction in labor. If anything, spicy foods can just cause a bit more discomfort during pregnancy, she says. “In the third trimester, spicy foods are more likely to cause heartburn or acid reflux, stomach discomfort, diarrhea, or intestinal cramping — especially if you’re not used to spicy foods — rather than actually starting labor,” Chuang says. Do Spicy Foods Pose Any Risk To Pregnancy? Both experts noted that there’s really no reason to avoid spicy foods during pregnancy. No evidence suggests that the heat is harmful. In fact, Callipari says, many spicy foods have health benefits. Capsaicin, the compound that gives hot peppers its heat, is a known bacteriostatic agent, meaning it inhibits the growth of bacteria. “It helps to fight infection,” Callipari explains, adding that people in cultures around the world continue to eat spicy foods across the duration of pregnancy. “It stops bacteria from growing. So spice was added a lot to our foods when we didn’t have a fridge thousands of years ago, but culturally we discovered that spicy foods are healthier foods because they lasted.” Chuang says that while pregnant people shouldn’t feel as though they need to stay away from those piquant bites, hot wings could irritate pre-existing hemorrhoids on top of any acid reflux or heartburn in the third trimester. “One rule for people to remember is that with spicy foods, you may feel the burn going in but also sometimes, coming out!” she says. Are There Any Particular Foods That Do, In Fact, Induce Labor? Like spicy foods, there are many things from eggplant to licorice that have been said to induce labor — few of which have any convincing evidence behind them, Chaung says. “Dates have some preliminary evidence but other popular choices like pineapple have not been shown to reliably start labor,” Chuang says. Chuang adds that she often recommends a smoothie of pineapple, coconut water, dates and agave nectar to patients as a fun, nutrient rich snack — it’s just not going to kickstart the birthing process. TLDR: It seems pretty safe to turn up the heat!

articles.title: In 2023, New York mother Casey McIntyre arranged a fundraiser to erase strangers' medical bills after her death; by December 2024, her memorial campaign had funded more than $120 million in debt relief
articles.summary: Before dying from stage four ovarian cancer at age 38, New York mother Casey McIntyre arranged a final message that turned her personal loss into
articles.body: Before dying from stage four ovarian cancer at age 38, New York mother Casey McIntyre arranged a final message that turned her personal loss into financial relief for tens of thousands of strangers across the United States. By December 2024, the viral memorial campaign created in her honor had raised millions of dollars. The money allowed non-profit organization Undue Medical Debt to erase more than $120 million (£90 million) in unpaid healthcare bills. McIntyre, a publishing executive who lived in Brooklyn with her husband, Andrew Gregory, and their young daughter, died in November 2023. Before her death, she worked with her husband to create a debt jubilee fundraiser through Undue Medical Debt, which was formerly called RIP Medical Debt. "To celebrate my life, I've decided to buy up medical debt and then destroy it," read the message posted to her social media accounts after her death, as released by Undue Medical Debt.Rapid public response generates millionsThe campaign quickly connected with donors around the world. Within weeks of McIntyre's death, donations poured into the special fundraising page. The campaign passed its first goals within hours. According to press releases from Undue Medical Debt, the campaign raised more than $1 million in direct donations during its opening phase. Because the charity buys groups of medical debts on secondary markets for pennies on the dollar, every donated dollar can erase about $100 in debt based on its original value. In December 2023, Undue Medical Debt announced its first major debt relief funded by McIntyre's campaign. The organization bought and erased $44.9 million in healthcare debt, helping more than 51,000 people across the country. Recipients received yellow envelopes in the mail telling them that their unpaid medical balances had been completely cleared. They were not given tax penalties or any other obligations.A second wave of debt cancellationAs donations continued to grow throughout 2024, the campaign reached another major milestone during the holiday season. In December 2024, Undue Medical Debt released a statement confirming that a second round of debt relief funded by McIntyre's campaign had erased more than $75 million in medical debt. Combined with the first round, the total amount of canceled healthcare debt passed $120 million, helping tens of thousands of low-income families. Andrew Gregory said his late wife understood that she had more access to healthcare treatment than many other people. That awareness helped motivate her to assist people facing financial hardship because of illness. "Casey was profoundly grateful for the excellent care she received, but she was also furious about how unjust the American healthcare system is," Gregory stated in press releases issued by Undue Medical Debt. "She wanted to make sure that others who were suffering wouldn't have to carry the added burden of crippling debt."Mechanism behind debt abolitionUndue Medical Debt works by buying groups of unpaid medical accounts from hospitals, health systems, and collection agencies. The non-profit focuses on debt held by people who earn four times or less than the federal poverty level, or whose medical debt equals 5 percent or more of their yearly gross income. After the organization buys the debt, it permanently cancels it instead of trying to collect the money. Allison Sesso, Chief Executive Officer of Undue Medical Debt, highlighted the effect McIntyre's campaign had on the organization's outreach work. "Casey's gift was a remarkable act of generosity that turned her family's grief into a powerful force for good," Sesso said in a statement published by the non-profit. "Her story touched a nerve because so many Americans know firsthand the crushing weight of medical debt."Continuing support for families in needThe campaign became one of the most successful fundraising efforts by a single person in the history of Undue Medical Debt. Beyond directly canceling debt, the attention around McIntyre's campaign encouraged other grassroots groups, faith organizations, and local governments to work with the non-profit. These groups sought to erase medical debt in their own communities. For Gregory and their daughter, Grace, the campaign created a meaningful way to honor McIntyre's memory. The fundraising page remains active, allowing people to keep donating to debt relief efforts in her name. The postal notices sent to recipients simply said that their debts had been cleared in memory of Casey McIntyre, a mother who wanted to make healthcare access less difficult for others.You use AI every day. articles.title: Howard Stern warns ABC will have 'hell to pay' if something 'goes wrong' with Jimmy Kimmel's show
articles.summary: Radio host Howard Stern warned Tuesday that ABC would have "hell to pay" should anything "go wrong" with "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" while appearing as a guest on the late-night show.
articles.body: Radio host Howard Stern told the "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" audience Tuesday that ABC would have "hell to pay" if something went wrong with late-night host Jimmy Kimmel's show. "I want to say something to ABC if they're watching right now," Stern said, noting he had previously heard rumors about the show and did not know what was true. "There is no man more loyal to this company than this guy. "And what I mean by that, this is the truth. For years, I've said to him, you know, he goes to these things. ABC has a corporate function where they try to attract advertisers. Every year, he'd go to what they call the upfronts." The radio host told the audience that Kimmel would always attend the events because ABC needed him to be there. BOB IGER BREAKS SILENCE ON DISNEY'S SUSPENSION OF JIMMY KIMMEL OVER CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION COMMENTS "He has done everything for the company. And I hope that they keep that in mind," he said. "Oh my God. I don't know about you, but if something goes wrong, oh, is ABC going to have hell to pay. Am I correct? Are you with me?" ABC did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Reports of Kimmel's show being canceled were dismissed by ABC earlier this month. A spokesperson pushed back on Page Six's report that Kimmel's contract would not be renewed, calling any reports about the future of the late-night show "speculative." KIMMEL REVEALS HE'S INTERVIEWING JAMES TALARICO UNDER 'UNUSUAL CIRCUMSTANCES,' CITING FCC THREATS "Howard Stern's reign as king of all media is over in more ways than one," Hollywood in Toto founder Christian Toto told Fox News Digital in a statement about Stern's remarks. "The man who once stood tall for free speech went silent during the woke culture wars. Now, he's rushing to a multi-millionaire's defense, someone whose show is likely costing ABC dearly. "That explains why the network needs a drastic budget reduction to keep ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’ on the air," he continued. "If CBS was losing $40 million a year to keep Stephen Colbert employed, imagine what ABC must swallow to appease Kimmel. "The old Stern would have recognized those basic business principles," Toto added. "The new version? He's an ultra-rich liberal supporting a fellow ultra-rich liberal while misleading the public on the issues in play." Kimmel's show was taken off-air briefly in September 2025 after remarks the late-night host made about Charlie Kirk's assassin. The liberal late-night personality returned to air a few days later and has referenced the suspension in frequent jabs directed at President Donald Trump, as well as Federal Communications Commission (FCC) chair Brendan Carr. Kimmel, after returning from his summer break on Sept. 8, jabbed at Carr and said, "We're still here." The late-night host noted that it was the 4,000th episode of "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" "We’ve done 4,000 of these. Which is, it’s a lot of shows," Kimmel said. "According to the White House, it’s too many shows. "There are those who said we would never last this long. There are even those who used the regulatory might of the FCC to unconstitutionally try to make sure we didn’t last this long. But we did it the hard way, Brendan. And we are still here." DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS The late-night host had New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on the show Monday night and questioned him repeatedly about the nature of his relationship with Trump. The democratic socialist mayor seemed to deflect Kimmel's questions as Mamdani avoided criticizing Trump and rejected the late-night host's request to send him a selfie. "Did you guys hit it off immediately or is it something that you really went into thinking, like, ‘OK, I need to have a relationship with the president of the United States, and I think the best way to do it is to charm him?' How did you do that and can you help me?" Kimmel asked Mamdani, calling his relationship with Trump "unexpected." Mamdani responded, "Sorry, brother." "The No. 1 thing that we've been speaking about recently has been Sunnyside Yard, which is this idea for decades of building a platform over a rail yard and then building 12,000 homes. And so, in that moment, you know, that you zoomed in on, I'm just thinking about 12,000 homes, 30,000 jobs, largest housing development since the early 1970s," Mamdani told Kimmel. Kimmel asked, "When you text him about Sunnyside, are you sure he doesn't think you're texting him about eggs?" Mamdani said he was "pretty sure" and noted that the texts were pretty normal and didn't resemble the president's Truth Social posts. "Wow. You really have broken through with him," Kimmel said. "I mean, listen, you seem to be doing a great job in New York. We might need you to move to Washington just hang out at the Oval Office all day. Like, if you texted him a selfie of us right now." MAMDANI SAYS EVEN IF HE CAN GET ALONG WITH TRUMP, HE STILL DEMANDS THAT 'ICE SHOULD BE ABOLISHED' Mamdani laughed and shut it down. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I love you, but I love housing more," Mamdani responded.

articles.title: ASU hockey coach is put on leave;  hospitalized player is unlikely to recover, family attorney says
articles.summary: Matthew Mayich, 21, collapsed during a workout in the hot Arizona sun on Aug. 20. and suffered extreme heatstroke.
articles.body: Arizona State University announced Wednesday it has put hockey coach Greg Powers on leave following the collapse of player Matthew Mayich during a summer team workout. Mayich, 21, remains on life support and is unlikely to recover, according to family attorney Rob Carey. In response to the announcement, Carey said in an interview with NBC Nightly News that the family has said “since day one” that the entire coaching staff needed to be put on administrative leave. ASU has left in place another assistant coach who is good friends with the head coach “and that needs to change,” the attorney said. “They did nothing right, literally nothing,” Carey said of the ASU coaching staff during the workout. “And as a result [of] what should have been a very preventable workout problem, heatstroke, a man is on life support and unlikely to come off of it,” he said. “He’s incapacitated, and there’s almost no chance of recovery. But the family’s very devout, and they want to give their son a chance for a miracle,” Carey said. ASU did not immediately respond to a request for comment from NBC News on the family’s allegations and demands for an independent investigation. But in its announcement on Powers’ leave, ASU Athletics Director Graham Rossini stated that the school’s “focus continues to be on Matthew and his family” and all student-athletes, to make sure they have “the support they need during this time and as the season begins.” “We have continued to collect as much information as possible. After thorough and careful deliberation, I believe this is the best move to provide stability for the hockey program,” Rossini said. Assistant Coach Mike Corbett will be leading the team this weekend for the season opener and an interim head coach would be named soon, according to the statement. Mayich collapsed during an outdoor workout on Aug. 20. He suffered extreme heatstroke and has been hospitalized since his collapse. Mayich’s parents, John and Christina Mayich, and seven other players from the hockey team called on Tuesday for coaches involved to be placed on leave and for an independent investigation. The seven players, who did not share their names, submitted through their attorney a letter to ASU President Michael Crow disputing the school’s account of what occurred. In the letter, the players said they were afraid of being retaliated against because the coaches “decide our playing time, scholarship levels, and roster status.” Although Carey said putting Powers on leave is a step in the right direction, he said there are players whose safety remains at risk and “retaliation is still possible.” The athletes’ 26-page letter describes a workout session led by Tim Ziesel, an Army veteran and former Green Beret, on a day the afternoon high temperature was 104 degrees and the low was 74, according National Weather Service data. The players alleged in their letter that Zeisel left before Mayich collapsed. According to the players, the workout did not include required emergency gear on site, including a tub of water for cooling off and a training plan had not been submitted to all the coaches. In its report, ASU said temperatures were between 86 and 89 degrees during the workout, with relative humidity between 51% and 46%. The ASU report also stated that an athletic trainer evaluated Mayich’s condition, put cool water and iced towels on him and told him to stay down; he then called 911 and directed student-athletes to help move him to the shade. Buddy Rake, Ziesel’s attorney, said Ziesel has offered to meet privately with Mayich’s family “and thinks a full and complete investigation should be done. “ “You have to find out what caused this. At the same time this workout is occurring, there’s probably 5,000 high school athletes in Arizona doing the same workout and nothing happens to them. So either the protocol is wrong, or there’s something else that happened,” Rake said. The players’ letter alleges the university’s temperature and humidity figures “understate conditions on the field.” The players noted that Mayich was new to Arizona, having been in the area for only eight days and having been involved in the hockey program for five. Drafted by the St. Louis Blues, Mayich is from Hamilton, Ontario, according to the NHL. The players said that Mayich got no water during a break that lasted only seconds, because he was one of several players who did not reach the water on time before they were “pushed directly into the next task.” The players said Powers characterized Mayich’s condition after his collapse as “just a little heat stroke” of the type he has seen before, according to their letter. Carey said putting staff on leave and hiring an outside investigator is fundamental when things such as this occur. In an interview with Canadian Broadcasting Company earlier this month, Mayich’s mother, Christina, said her son “was so excited to come to ASU — he said the facilities are even better live, because we watch it on YouTube and pictures and he just said it’s exciting.” She said they’re taking her son’s situation “day by day.” “Anybody who could send prayers for Matthew, it would be greatly appreciated because right now that’s what we need,” Christina Mayich said.
